# Ketch promo music bed: cue sheet

<!-- Generated by art/promo/audio/make_music.py from src/timing.json. Do not edit by hand:
     change the score (audio/score.py) or the timing and run audio/make-music.sh. -->

`music.wav` is an original track synthesized from scratch by `art/promo/audio/` (no samples or third-party audio), so it is royalty-free and falls under the repository's license. It is mastered for the film: mount it unchanged at volume 1. How it is built and how to change it: `art/promo/audio/README.md`.

| | |
|---|---|
| File | `public/audio/music.wav`, 48 kHz, 24-bit PCM, stereo |
| Length | exactly 77.000 s = 3,696,000 samples = 2310 frames at 30 fps |
| Timing | `src/timing.json`: 12 scenes, lane wipes at frames 120, 960, 1740, 2070 |
| Tempo | 120 BPM, 4/4. One beat = 0.5 s = 15 frames, one bar = 2 s = 60 frames. Every cut is on a beat |
| Key | D major / B minor |
| Loudness | -16.0 LUFS integrated, LRA 4.1 LU, true peak -1.4 dBTP, sample peak -1.57 dBFS |
| Ends | starts at digital silence, fades to digital silence at 77.000 s |

## Mounting in Remotion

Sample 0 is frame 0 of `Promo`. Put the audio at the root of `Promo` with no offset, trim or fade (both fades are in the file), for example
`<Audio src={staticFile('audio/music.wav')} />`, with `MUSIC = true` in `src/config.ts`. Do not mount it inside a scene `<Sequence>`: every cue below uses global frames.

## Picture ties

Most cues follow the cuts in `src/timing.json`. These follow animation inside a scene, so the score copies numbers from the scene code (`PICTURE_TIES` in `audio/score.py`). When you change one in the scene, change it in the score too and regenerate; `npm run music -- --check` compares them.

| score.py | value | scene code | the music |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SAIL_AT` | 0 | `src/scenes/S01Intro.tsx`: `SAIL_AT` | S01: the sail starts refilling; its segment refills carry the sparkle bells |
| `SAIL_TRACK_LEAD` | 6 | `src/components/SailLogo.tsx`: `SAIL_TIMING.trackLead` | S01: frames from the refill start to the first segment refill and its sparkle bell |
| `SAIL_STAGGER` | 3 | `src/components/SailLogo.tsx`: `SAIL_TIMING.stagger` | S01: frames between segment refills, one sparkle bell each |
| `SAIL_MAIN_ROWS + SAIL_MIZZEN_ROWS` | 10 | `src/components/SailLogo.tsx`: `SAIL_SEGMENTS` (matches of `\bseg\(`) | S01: one sparkle note per sail segment (SPARKLE_NOTES) |
| `SAIL_MIZZEN_ROWS` | 4 | `src/components/SailLogo.tsx`: `SAIL_SEGMENTS` (matches of `,\s*true\s*,?\s*\)`) | S01: the last segments, the mizzen's, get softer sparkle bells |
| `S01_WORD_AT` | 54 | `src/scenes/S01Intro.tsx`: `WORD_AT` | S01: the refill wave has crossed the sail; the low thump lands 6 frames later, on the held lock-up |
| `ROLL_32NDS_BEATS` | 2 | `src/scenes/S11Languages.tsx`: `ROLL_32NDS_BEATS` | S11: the snare roll goes to 32nds this many beats before S12, where the language ticker lands its last name |
| `S12_END_CARD_AT` | 105 | `src/scenes/S12OpenSource.tsx`: `CHORD` | S12: the end card lands on the final chord (the music splits into S12a and S12b there) |

## Sound

Pads are detuned band-limited saws through a state-variable low-pass; arp and bass are saw plucks with filter envelopes; bells are two-operator FM kept below 16.5 kHz (no aliasing); the sub is one continuous sine with a little second harmonic, sidechained to the kick; drums, whooshes and risers are pitched sines and filtered noise. Space comes from two convolution reverbs with synthetic impulse responses. The master has a 25 Hz high-pass, soft-knee saturation and a 4x oversampled look-ahead true-peak limiter (at most 0.44 dB of gain reduction, on 0.5 % of samples). Mono fold-down loses 0.8 LU.

## Regenerating

```sh
npm run music   # in art/promo; runs audio/make-music.sh
```

It sets up `art/promo/.venv` from `audio/requirements.txt` on first use, writes `public/audio/music.wav` and this file, and prints the measurements. The output is deterministic (fixed seeds; the same file byte for byte on every run).
